questions.text: Let [latex]A[/latex] and [latex]B[/latex] be any two arbitrary events, then, which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)\le P(A)+P(B)[/latex] always holds. The other options need extra conditions (independence or disjointness), or are wrong formulas.

Answer: [latex]P(A\cup B)\le P(A)+P(B)[/latex]

questions.text: If the ordinary generating function of a sequence [latex]\{a_{n}\}_{n=0}^{\infty} \;  is \;  \frac{1+z}{(1-z)^{3}}[/latex] then [latex]a_{3}-a_{0}[/latex] is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
[latex](1-z)^{-3}=\sum\binom{n+2}{2}z^n[/latex], so [latex]a_n=\binom{n+2}{2}+\binom{n+1}{2}[/latex].

[latex]a_3=10+6=16[/latex], [latex]a_0=1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_3-a_0=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.text:
For any discrete random variable X, with probability mass function
[latex]P(X=j)=p_{j}, p_{j}\geq 0, j \in \{0,....N\}[/latex] and [latex] \sum_{j=0}^{N}p_{j}=1[/latex], define the polynomial function [latex]g_{x}(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{N}p_{j}z^{j}[/latex]. For a certain discrete random variable Y, there exists a scalar [latex]\beta \in [/latex][0,1] such that [latex]g_{Y}(z)=(1-\beta +\beta z)^{N}[/latex]. The expectation of Y is
questions.solution:
For a pgf, [latex]E[Y]=g_Y'(1)[/latex]:
[latex]g_Y'(z)=N\beta(1-\beta+\beta z)^{N-1}\Rightarrow g_Y'(1)=N\beta[/latex]

(Y is Binomial(N, [latex]\beta[/latex]).)

Answer: [latex]N\beta[/latex]

questions.text:
P and Q are considering to apply for a job. The probability that P applies for the job is 1/4.
The probability that P applies for the job given that Q applies for the job is 1/2
, and the probability that Q applies for the job given that P applies for the job 1/3.
Then the probability that P does not apply for the job given that Q does not apply for the job is
questions.solution:
[latex]P(P\cap Q)=P(P)\,P(Q|P)=\frac14\cdot\frac13=\frac1{12}[/latex], and [latex]P(Q)=\frac{P(P\cap Q)}{P(P|Q)}=\frac16[/latex].

[latex]P(\bar P\cap\bar Q)=1-\left(\frac14+\frac16-\frac1{12}\right)=\frac23[/latex], [latex]P(\bar Q)=\frac56[/latex]

[latex]P(\bar P|\bar Q)=\frac{2/3}{5/6}=\frac45[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac45[/latex]

questions.text:
G is undirected graph with n vertices and 25 edges such that each vertex of G has degree at
least 3. Then the maximum possible value of n is ___________.
questions.solution:
Sum of degrees = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 25 = 50. Each vertex has degree [latex]\ge3[/latex], so [latex]3n\le50\Rightarrow n\le16[/latex].

Answer: 16
